title: Coherent formal modules Coh(X, I), the completion functor, and systems with support proper over a base
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] whose underlying space is quasi-compact) and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals (the ideal sheaf of a closed subscheme [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]). $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)$ denotes the full subcategory of the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] whose objects are the coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent]. (0) (Notation.) For a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ and an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$, $\mathcal J\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal F$ is the image of the multiplication map $\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$, $a\otimes s\mapsto as$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] (the subsheaf generated by the local sections $as$, $a$ a local section of $\mathcal J$, $s$ of $\mathcal F$); $\mathcal J^1=\mathcal J$ and $\mathcal J^{n+1}=\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal J^n$; $\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ is the cokernel of the inclusion $\mathcal J\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$. (1) $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is the category whose objects are inverse systems $(\mathcal F_n)_{n\ge1}$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules with $\mathcal O_X$-linear transition maps $\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$ such that $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_n=0$ and the transition map induces an isomorphism $\mathcal F_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$, for every $n\ge1$; a morphism $(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$ is a family of $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps $\alpha_n:\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal G_n$ commuting with the transition maps. (2) The *completion functor* $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ sends a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ to $\mathcal F^\wedge=(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)_{n\ge1}$ with the canonical surjections as transition maps, and an $\mathcal O_X$-linear $u:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ to $u^\wedge=(u\bmod\mathcal I^n)_n$. (3) For a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_X$, an object $(\mathcal F_n)$ is *annihilated by $\mathcal K$* if $\mathcal K\mathcal F_n=0$ for all $n$; it is *annihilated by a power of $\mathcal I$* ($\mathcal I$-power torsion) if it is annihilated by $\mathcal I^c$ for some $c\ge1$, which holds if and only if the transition maps $\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal F_c$ are isomorphisms for all $n\ge c$ (Stacks' formulation); for a closed subscheme $Z\subseteq X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_Z$, $(\mathcal F_n)$ is *supported on $Z$* if it is annihilated by $\mathcal I_Z$ (likewise a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ is supported on $Z$ if $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal F=0$). (4) If moreover $f:X\to S$ is a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $\mathit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }S}(X,\mathcal I)$ is the full subcategory of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ of the objects $(\mathcal F_n)$ such that $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_1)$ (a closed subset of $X$) is proper over $S$, and $\mathit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }S}(\mathcal O_X)$ is the full subcategory of $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)$ of the coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules with support proper over $S$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]; since $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F/\mathcal I\mathcal F)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$, the completion functor maps the second subcategory into the first.

proof.text: The existing image definitions give the ideal-module product and its monomorphic inclusion. Induction on the recursively constructed powers gives inclusions of higher powers into lower ones, including I^0 = O. The source isQuasicoherent_toModules proves that I is quasi-coherent. Tensor quasi-coherence and kernel/cokernel closure prove that the image product is quasi-coherent; induction gives quasi-coherence of every power.

Use formalModuleQuotient_factor: multiplication naturality and the power inclusions induce maps on images by Mathlib image.map. All quotient-map identities and composites follow by canceling their cokernel projections, as in the already proved formalModuleQuotientMap_id and formalModuleQuotientMap_comp.

For coherent F, use isCoherent_iff_isQuasicoherent_and_isFiniteType to obtain quasi-coherence and finite type. Quasi-coherence of I^n F and cokernel closure give quasi-coherence of F/I^n F. Restrict finite local generating sections along the quotient projection: overFunctor preserves epimorphisms and GeneratingSections.ofEpi retains the finite index sets. Thus the quotient is of finite type, and the coherence criterion proves it coherent.

The full subcategory of inverse systems with the stated coherent adic conditions is the existing CoherentFormalModule category; morphisms, identities and composition are inherited from the functor category.

Use the source monoidalClosed structure, whose tensor-left functors preserve epimorphisms. Multiplication naturality and cancellation of the tensor of the quotient projection show that a map out of a quotient kills its ideal product exactly when its composite with the projection kills the original ideal product. First this proves I^n(F/I^n F)=0. Then it constructs maps in both directions between (F/I^m F)/I^n(F/I^m F) and F/I^n F for n ≤ m using cokernel.desc. Cancellation of the quotient projections proves the two maps inverse; cokernel.π_desc identifies the forward composite with formalModuleQuotientMap. Specialize to m=n+2 and exponent n+1 to establish the adjacent transition condition.

The existing quotient-map identity and composition theorems give formalCompletionSystem_laws and formalCompletionMap_naturality. Componentwise NatTrans.ext gives formalCompletionMap_laws, yielding the existing completion functor by ObjectProperty.lift.

For fixed c, factor inclusions of all higher-power products through I^(c+1) to transfer uniform annihilation. The inclusion defining each successive quotient above c is therefore zero, so CokernelCofork.IsColimit.isIso_π and the given quotient isomorphism imply that successive transition maps are isomorphisms. Induction on c ≤ n and functoriality give the transition to level c. Conversely the given isomorphisms to level c are monomorphisms; multiplication naturality transfers annihilation of level c to each n ≥ c, since image inclusion and factorThruImage detect zero multiplication. For n < c, factor the I^(c+1) product through the already zero I^(n+1) product.

Retain the existing proof of proper support: exactness of the stalk functor makes each stalk quotient of a zero stalk zero, hence support of F/IF lies inside that of F. The coherent finite-type criterion and module_support_proper_over_base make its support closed. Apply the downward-closure clause of closed_subset_proper_over_base_properties and lift the completion functor to the proper-support subcategories.

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks coherent.tex Section 0EHN (section-coherent-formal), equation 0880 (equation-completion-functor), the paragraph before Lemma 0889 (lemma-existence-easy), the proof of Theorem 088E, Section 0CYW and equation 088D (all tags verified in tags/tags). Statement made well formed: it used I^n F_n and F/I^nF without defining them, so part (0) defines JF as the image of J (x) F -> F (as Stacks does in the proof of Lemma 01YP), J^n and the quotient, and Coh(O_X) as a full subcategory of O_X-modules; added def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product and def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category to stmt_deps. The node's 'annihilated by K' (K F_n = 0 for all n) differs in form from Stacks' 'annihilated by I^c' (F_n = F_c for n >= c); the equivalence is now stated in (3) and proved in step 7. Eight steps: JF and J^n quasi-coherent with affine sections J(U)F(U) (from the tensor and image nodes); reduction to affine opens; F/JF coherent (01XZ via pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth, a tool lemma of unit sk-prop-av-pqf-finite already accepted as tool_use on lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent); Coh(X,I) a category; F^ an object; completion a functor; (3) with the Stacks equivalence; (4) closedness of supports, fullness, Supp(F/IF) in Supp(F) and 0CYN (lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties (2)). No new nodes needed: every claim is either elementary or an existing node; abelianness (087X), exactness (0881), Serre property (0CYV/0CYU) and the i_* description of 'supported on Z' (087T) are separate nodes or not part of the definition. Mathlib has no coherent modules, no ideal-times-module sheaf; searches added. No Lean in slopmaster2 (grep of WeilConjectures for coherent formal / adic systems / completion functor: none).
